evidence.source: 中央研究院漢字古今文字資料庫
evidence.text: The record shows 明 in oracle-bone, bronze, Chu manuscript, seal, and Shuowen ancient-script categories; its accompanying account analyzes 明 as 日+月 for brightness. The record identifies a bronze example by 集成00161. This supports the 日月 analysis but does not establish that it was the only early graphic analysis.
evidence.title: 漢字「明」：字形演變

evidence.source: Taiwan Ministry of Education, Dictionary of Chinese Character Variants
evidence.field: 說文釋形；字樣說明；釋義
evidence.text: The dictionary reports that Shuowen's standard seal form is 朙, analyzed as 月 plus 囧, glossed ‘照也’ (illuminate). It describes 日/月 as the ancient-script form of 朙. It also gives the reading míng and cites the Shijing line 東方明矣, 朝既昌矣, illustrating an early dawn/daybreak use. This documents Shuowen's historical analysis, not proof of the word's original sense.
evidence.title: A01784 明 — Ministry of Education Dictionary of Chinese Character Variants

evidence.field: 形義通解；甲骨文及金文用例
evidence.text: The entry reports four oracle-bone forms: 日+月, interpreted by Xu Zhongshu as the sun rising while the moon remains, hence dawn; 月+囧, with 囧 also phonetic and depicted as a lattice window, interpreted as moonlight entering a room; 目+月, with the oracle-bone examples too fragmentary to confirm as 明; and 田+月, where 田 may be a corruption of 日 or 囧. It says oracle-bone examples include dawn in 合集481 (‘乙巳明雨’) and brightness in 合集21037 (‘不喪朙’). Bronze examples include dawn in 大盂鼎, and ‘clear/manifest’ uses in other inscriptions. The entry reports that the Qin Shuihudi manuscript’s 目-form was judged by Qiu Xigui to be a corruption of 囧. It separately records 明 borrowed for ‘next’ in a Tsinghua manuscript and as a loan for 盟 in Houma covenant texts. These are source-reported readings and interpretations; the underlying inscription images were not inspected here.
evidence.title: 漢語多功能字庫 — 明

evidence.source: Wiktionary-hosted Baxter–Sagart table; local transcription cross-check
evidence.field: Old Chinese readings; sources/baxter-sagart/baxtersagart.tsv rows 1755 and 2357
evidence.text: The local Baxter–Sagart dataset gives 囧 *k-mraŋʔ (with dialect note *k.mr- > *kʷr-) and 明 *mraŋ. These are distinct readings in the same Old Chinese reconstruction system; the initial and final differ, so the table alone does not demonstrate a sound match between 囧 and 明. The CUHK entry's claim that 囧 also functions phonetically is a separate source assertion. Local rows checked: 囧 row 1755, 明 row 2357. Dataset notation retained as printed.
evidence.title: 囧 — Old Chinese pronunciation (table checked against local Baxter–Sagart dataset)

gaps: The exact phonetic relation remains unresolved: Baxter–Sagart gives 明 *mraŋ and 囧 *k-mraŋʔ, while CUHK describes 囧 as phonetic in the 月+囧 form. No independently inspected primary phonological source establishes how the phonetic analysis accounts for this difference or dates that relationship.

The account that 囧 depicts a lattice window is reported by CUHK; this research did not independently establish 囧's earliest referent or recover the object's spoken name. Since the proposed relation is a component role within 明 rather than a whole-graph loan, uncertainty about the object name does not by itself decide the phonetic analysis.

No inscription image was visually inspected; ancient-form chronology and readings are reported from the dictionary account. Exact dating of the individual oracle-bone and bronze examples was not established in this pass.

Official Unihan character pages could not be accessed, so the required external click-through verification of current Mandarin readings is incomplete. Local Unihan kMandarin rows show 明 míng and 囧 jiǒng, but are not external evidence.

The early sense chronology is not fully resolved. Sources support both dawn and illumination/brightness uses in oracle-bone material; the graphic forms and gloss list do not establish which semantic use preceded the other.
